TT is dominant, while Tt in recessive. If something is dominant, they will pass it on to their offspring 100%, with recessive it'd be lower in chances. If you're planning to design the genotype yourself, some knowledge of genetics may come in handy. For this, we recommend looking at horse genetics to give yourself a head start. 6288: Hi Loudish sorry for the bother but Essence is EE black, so shouldn't all the pups turn out as Ee?
Black works a bit different than the rest of the genes, and unfortunately an Ee is never guaranteed out of an EE black.

ahhh meeeeen, seriously? are these rules written somewhere? 
We paid a fortune to buy that EE black baby just in the hope of guaranteed blacks. :/ 
It is really not clear that there are genes which work differently. :/ You guys should make an exclusion list of these matters. It is really annoying that we actually paid loads for an ordinary black.

It has been stated several times in the past yes, that breeding blacks to tawnies will never result in black puppies, regardless of whether the black is EE or Ee. Tokotas have their very own genetic system that is, for the most part, unrelated to other genetic systems in how the genes are passed.

I've taken these comments from the Breeding and Genotypes Guide , which is posted publicly to the group, where people have had similar confusions; 

 comments.deviantart.com/1/5586… 

 comments.deviantart.com/1/5586… 

And this comment, from the Genetics and Mutations journal which has been posted to the group since the very beginning:

 comments.deviantart.com/1/4612… 

As you can see, EE blacks do not guarantee the passing of E in any breeding. Since Tokotas are primarily meant to be a light-coloured species, breeding Black is designed to be harder than breeding, say, a Tundra or a Tawny. It's always a good idea to scroll through the comments of the genetics journals if you're unsure of something, as many others have likely had the same questions answered by the admins.

9030: The Dam is an EE black, and the Sire is a Tt tundra; shouldn't they all be black?
EE black bred to a tundra still only has a small chance of passing black as the coat color unfortunately. Even though it's dominant, it won't always bring blacks ;-;/
When was that rule passed? Last time I bred an EE black to a Tt tundra the Dom EE passed as a Dom trait.

It isn't a rule at all, it's always been that way ^^ We have a coded roller that contains all the specs for inputting our breedings. Based on the coding and the genos between the two parents as well as other factors such as items/companions, it rolls a random amount of pups and uses the genos of the two parents to create the puppies genotypes (more common ones show up more often, and rarer ones show up less often). It's just one of those you may get lucky, you may not sort of things.

It's just best to breed blacks with Aa browns or other blacks if you really want black puppies since they have the highest chances ;-;

Blac k is rolled as a mutation of sorts, even if you have an EE tokota, and breed it to an Aa or Tt, you won't always get black. Its a small percentage chance - making black the most rare of base coats. If you had a breeding that resulted in all blacks you are extremely lucky, but it has always been this way, nothing has changed. Also please note the group if you have questions next time, no other comments beside litters and owner transfers should be here.

Tokotines 2020 Exchange Alaktiq wondered, briefly, why Tanoka had laughed when he told him where he was going today. The smaller dire had seemed to insinuate that he knew something that Alaktiq did not, but no matter how he pondered, Alaktiq had no idea what Tanoka could have been talking about. Kettle had been no help either, flicking his tail nonchalantly when Alaktiq had looked at him for assistance. 
Well, Talis had encouraged him to meet new tokotas, particularly other dires, and when Arianwen had mentioned offhandedly that she could introduce him to Daenerys, Talis had encouraged him to go. He wasn't sure why they all thought he'd need encouragement; it was always fun to meet new tokotas, and he wasn't like Tanoka, always pretending to be grumpy and put out by the presence of others. That wasn't really true anyway; Tanoka was really just a big sweetheart who liked to pretend he wasn't. But he always grumbled about meeting new tokotas, while he, Alaktiq, was almost always up for more socialization.
